title: Home
text: Introduction This Implementation Guide (IG) is provided by MedCom to describe the use of FHIR ®© in message based exchange of data in Danish healthcare. Scope of the messaging framework MedCom has profiled the HL7 FHIR Messaging Framework to work in a Danish context. Governance for MedCom HL7 FHIR Messaging describes the basic ruleset of how MedCom Messages must be exchanged in the Danish Healthcare Messaging Network. The Danish ruleset is based on: the ruleset for the Danish VANS Network the general HL7 FHIR Communication Rules for FHIR Messaging the Danish profiling of FHIR messaging. These MedCom FHIR Messaging Governance rules are intended to clarify the use of MedCom’s FHIR messages for the health and social area. Formerly, these kinds of rules for other MedCom Messaging paradigms were known as ”Syntax & Communication Rules”. It is the intention that the MedCom FHIR Messaging Governance rules together with MedCom’s FHIR standards for the individual messages form the full and sufficient basis for implementing MedCom’s healthcare messages. General Messaging Model The figure below illustrates a general messaging model, which all MedCom messages will comply to. Messaging profiles are all prefixed "MedComMessaging". Beside the profiles on the figure, a MedCom message will also include some MedComCore profiles and profiles made to support a specific use case. All together they constitute the actual content of a MedCom message. The following sections describe the overall purpose of each messaging profile. MedComMessagingMessage A Bundle resource defined to be of the type 'message'. All profiles included in a message shall be referenced from the entry element in the MedComMessagingMessage profile, with a MessageHeader as the first resource. Note: Be aware that entries in a message in general are unordered. Recipients of a message cannot assume any sequences of profiles. MedComMessagingMessageHeader The MessageHeader defines the sender and receiver organization of a message. In some messages it is optional to include a one or more carbon-copy receiver organization(s). From the focus element is the actual content of the message often referenced, like a Communication or Encounter resource. MedComMessagingOrganization This profile inherits from MedComCoreOrganization and is used to describe a sender and receiver organization. The resource constrains the MedComCoreOrganization profile to contain both a SOR identifier and an EAN identifier (also known as GLN) for addressing purposes. MedComMessagingProvenance The Provenance resource describes the activity of the message and who has triggered the message. Further is it used to describes the history of message activities e.g., if the message is related to a previously exchanged message. In the table below, each term or abbreviation has an associated description that eloborates the meaning of the term. For some terms is a link provided, which includes more information about the term. title: Message Exchange
text: Governance for MedCom FHIR Message Exchange MedCom FHIR messaging uses asynchronous exchange through the Danish healthcare messaging network. This guidance also applies to corresponding OIOXML versions where the FHIR message defines their content. MedCom exchange model Asynchronous messaging A sending system dispatches a message to a receiving system through the messaging network. The response is returned asynchronously. Addressing in the VANS network uses the organization information held in SOR; see VANS network governance . The Bundle , MessageHeader , and Provenance profiles own the message structure, identifiers, timestamps, routing references, and history requirements. For the general exchange framework and response patterns, see FHIR messaging . Reliable Messaging MedCom Reliable Messaging combines acknowledgements, retries, and duplicate detection. A missing acknowledgement leaves the sender uncertain: either the message or its acknowledgement may have been lost. Retrying must therefore be safe even when the receiver has already processed the message. Two acknowledgement layers Layer What the acknowledgement confirms VANSEnvelope The receiving transport handler's result for the envelope. This does not confirm that the FHIR application accepted its content. FHIR message The receiving application's result: acceptance (AA), error (AE), or rejection (AR). Only AA marks the message as successfully sent and received; AE and AR mark it as failed. On the VANS network, each MedCom FHIR message SHALL be carried in a VANSEnvelope with reliable transport enabled: VANSEnvelope/Message/MetaInformation/Transport/Type is reliable or omitted (the default). See VANS network requirements . Both primary and copy receivers SHALL return a FHIR Acknowledgement for each non-Acknowledgement message. Its MessageHeader.response.identifier quotes the original MessageHeader.id . A FHIR Acknowledgement SHALL NOT itself receive a FHIR Acknowledgement; its envelope still uses reliable transport. Rules to make Reliable Messaging work FHIR Messaging rules AA = Application Accept & AE = Application Error & AR = Application Reject. You can read more in the Acknowledgement IG . ID Rule MR1.S A MedCom FHIR Acknowledgement SHALL be requested on a FHIR Message MR2.S A MedCom FHIR Message SHALL be marked as sent and received when an AA Acknowledgement has been received MR3.S A MedCom FHIR Message SHALL be marked as failed when an AR, or AE Acknowledgement has been received MR6.R A MedCom FHIR Message SHALL NOT be resent if an AE Acknowledgement has been received MR7.R A MedCom FHIR Message that is resent SHALL be updated with a new Bundle.id , Bundle.timestamp and Provenance timestamps MR8.R A MedCom FHIR Message is considered a duplicate if it contains the same MessageHeader.Id as a previously received MedCom FHIR Message MR9.R A duplicate MedCom FHIR Message SHALL NOT have different business content compared to the original message FHIR Messaging Acnowledgement rules ID Rules KR1.R A FHIR message SHALL be acknowledged KR2.R An Acknowledgement message SHALL not be acknowledged KR3.R If no errors are found while receiving a message, an AA Acknowledgement SHALL be sent KR4.R If a technical error occurs in the receiver's system while receiving a message, an AR Acknowledgement SHALL be sent KR5.R If a technical error from KR4.R is resolved and the message can be loaded. An AA Acknowledgement SHALL be sent KR6.R If a message validates negatively against the standard's profiling, it SHALL be acknowledged negatively with an AE Acknowledgement KR7.S If an Acknowledgement of a message is not received within 30 minutes, the original message MAY be marked for resending Sending scenarios The primary receiver is the main recipient of a message. A copy receiver receives a separate message based on the message sent to the primary receiver. The scenarios below distinguish between two ways to send a copy: Type When it is used Business content Carbon copy (CC) The copy receiver is known when the original message is prepared and sent. The same as the message sent to the primary receiver. Forward The message is sent later to a receiver who was not included in the original exchange. Most of the original content is retained; minor changes are allowed, subject to the clarification in Scenario #4. In these scenarios, “message” means a MedComMessagingMessage. Each carbon copy or forward is a new message with its own identifiers and message history. Scenario #1: Sending to a primary receiver Use this scenario when sending a new message, replying to a message, withdrawing a message, or sending a correction to the primary receiver. For example, a hospital sends a new message to a general practitioner. The practitioner is the primary receiver, and the sending activity is new-message . The sender SHALL include a MedComMessagingProvenance resource that records the sending activity using one of these codes: Activity code Use it when new-message Sending a new message. reply-message Replying to a previous message. retract-message Withdrawing a previous message. modified-message Sending a corrected or updated version of a previous message. Scenario #2: Creating a carbon copy or forward Use this scenario whenever another receiver needs a carbon copy or a forwarded message. The same preparation steps apply to both; Scenarios #3 and #4 describe their specific requirements. For example, a hospital sends a message to a general practitioner and also needs to send a carbon copy to a municipality. The municipality receives a separate message with its own identifiers. The sending application SHALL create a copy of the original message and send it as a new MedComMessagingMessage. Give the new message its own MessageHeader.id and Bundle.id , and set its dispatch timestamp according to the message identity and acknowledgement requirements and Bundle identifier and dispatch-time requirements . Add a new MedComMessagingProvenance resource. It SHALL describe the copy or forward activity and be added to the message history . Scenario #3: Sending when the carbon-copy receivers are already known Use this scenario when the sender knows the primary receiver and the carbon-copy receivers before sending the original message. Every message sent in this exchange SHALL list both the primary destination and all carbon-copy destinations. This lets every receiver see who the main recipient is and who receives a copy. For example, a hospital sends a message to a general practitioner and a carbon copy to a municipality. Both messages list the practitioner as the primary receiver and the municipality as a carbon-copy receiver. Scenario #3a: Sending the carbon copy For each carbon-copy receiver in Scenario #3, prepare a separate message using the steps in Scenario #2. The carbon copy SHALL contain the same content as the message sent to the primary receiver, except for its new Bundle.id , new MessageHeader.id , and additional MedComMessagingProvenance resource. Dispatch timestamps follow the requirements linked in Scenario #2. Assign the new identifiers. All other MessageHeader content SHALL NOT be changed, including the primary and carbon-copy destinations. Add a Provenance entry for the copy activity, following the Provenance history requirements . All other bundled resources SHALL NOT be changed. Create a VANSEnvelope for this copy. It SHALL use the carbon-copy receiver's GLN as the receiving EAN. In the example above, the carbon copy still lists the practitioner as primary receiver and the municipality as copy receiver. Its VANSEnvelope addresses the municipality so that the copy is delivered there. Scenario #4: Forwarding a message Use this scenario when a message is sent later to a new receiver who was not included when the original message was prepared and sent. For example, a general practitioner receives a hospital message and later forwards it to a municipality that was not a receiver of the original message. A forward is a new MedComMessagingMessage. It SHALL retain most of the original content and MAY contain minor adjustments or minor new content. It MAY also copy the original content without changes, apart from the new identifiers and additional Provenance resource. Create the new message as described in Scenario #2, with a new Bundle.id and MessageHeader.id . All other MessageHeader content SHALL NOT be changed. Add a Provenance entry for the forward activity, following the Provenance history requirements . All other bundled resources SHALL NOT be changed. Create a VANSEnvelope for the forward. It SHALL use the new receiver's GLN as the receiving EAN. The new receiver is therefore addressed in the VANSEnvelope, while the MessageHeader retains the original destinations. Clarification needed: The forwarding rules allow minor content changes but also prohibit changes to other bundled resources. These requirements need to be reconciled to define which content may be changed. Receiving scenarios A system can receive a MedComMessagingMessage as either the primary receiver or a copy receiver. For example, in Scenario #3, the general practitioner receives the primary message and the municipality receives the carbon copy. The receiver's role as primary receiver or copy receiver SHALL be recorded in Provenance. Both primary and copy receivers SHALL generate and send a MedCom Acknowledgement for each message other than an Acknowledgement. Each receiver acknowledges the separate message delivered to it. For example, the practitioner acknowledges the primary message, and the municipality acknowledges its copy. An Acknowledgement message does not receive another FHIR Acknowledgement; see Two acknowledgement layers .

title: Validation Governance
text: FHIR Messaging - Validation Governance Sender-side validation The sender SHALL provide valid outgoing FHIR messages according to the relevant FHIR Implementation Guide(s) (IG) before transmission. This includes Acknowledgements. Messages with validation errors SHALL NOT be sent unless explicitly approved by the responsible authority within the sending organization. Receiver-side validation Standards released after 2025, you will be able to read the version of the standard through the MessageDefinition. You can find it in the MessageHeader via the definition element .e.g. "definition" : "http://medcomfhir.dk/ig/messagedefinitions/MessageDefinition/MedComCareCommunicationMessageDefinition|5.0" . Everything after the pipe | symbol is the version of the standard. You should only care about the major and minor semantic version. If the pipe also has a patch, ignore it. The receiver SHALL ensure the validity of the received incoming messages according to the relevant FHIR Implementation Guide(s) (IG) before further processing. Receivers SHALL accept non-critical warnings but SHALL reject messages that violate mandatory constraints and rules. The sender SHALL ensure the validity of the received incoming acknowledgements and ensure that they correctly reference the original message. If an Acknowledgement is not valid, the receiver SHALL contact the sending system through alternative communication channels to inform them that their acknowledgement messages are not conformant. If no version has been specificed, the receiver SHOULD try and validate with the newest version of the standard. If that doesn't work, then the next-newest, until all major versions have been tried.

title: Vans Network Layer
text: Governance for the VANS Network Layer The Danish Healthcare Messaging Network is currently the VANS Network on which the overall shipment of a message is handled through Asynchronous Messaging. To be able to communicate over the VANS Network, both senders and receivers SHALL have a GLN number issued by the SOR. Click here to open SOR . The SOR is developed by The Danish Health Data Authority and therefore the information in SOR are in Danish. To be able to communicate a specific MedCom FHIR message type both senders and receivers SHALL be registered in SOR with that message type and version. The Sending Ecosystem SHALL validate the message before dispatching it. Validating a message SHALL include validating the correct use of the ValueSets and CodeSystems used in the message. VANSEnvelope VANSEnvelope carries XML-based and other non-EDIFACT message types over the VANS network. Unless the individual standard specifies otherwise, MedCom FHIR messages SHALL be sent in a VANSEnvelope, whether encoded as application/fhir+xml or application/fhir+json . Reception may use VANSEnvelope or another envelope, such as KOMBIT's BeskedFordeler envelope. Envelopment SHALL follow the VANSEnvelope specification (Danish) and the metadata requirements below. Each VANSEnvelope SHALL contain only one MedCom FHIR message. Payload and transport metadata The FHIR message SHALL be base64-encoded in VANSEnvelope/Message/Data/ . Under VANSEnvelope/Message/MetaInformation/Transport , TransformMessage is handled as usual. ServiceTag with the attribute name="MCM:MIME" SHALL contain application/fhir+xml or application/fhir+json , matching the message's encoding. Document metadata The following fields are under VANSEnvelope/Message/MetaInformation/Document/ : Format Format SHALL match "Standard type" in MedCom's Standards Directory and SHALL be HL7 for all FHIR standards. Name Name SHALL match "Type nr." in MedCom's Standards Directory and SHALL be prefixed with MCM: . It may include a statistical suffix identifying a message variant, as with GGOP1, GGOP2, and GGOP3. The FHIR-specific names and suffixes are listed below. Version Version SHALL match "Version" in MedCom's Standards Directory and therefore depends on the message type and version. MedCom FHIR message types Message type Sending envelope Receiving envelope Name Version Allowed postfix values CareCommunication VANSEnvelope VANSEnvelope MCM:FDIS91#<postfix value> 5.0 CareCommunication categories HospitalNotification VANSEnvelope (EPJ) KOMBIT's BeskedFordeler envelope (EOJ and other municipal systems) MCM:FDIS20#<postfix value> 3.0.0 HospitalNotification activity codes Acknowledgement VANSEnvelope VANSEnvelope MCM:FCTL#<postfix value> 2.0 FHIR response codes For CareCommunication and HospitalNotification, Name SHALL be taken from MedComMessagingSorEdiSystem . For Acknowledgement, Name SHALL be taken from VansStatisticalCodeCombination . For each type, postfix values SHALL come from the linked value set, and the combined name and postfix SHALL conform to VansStatisticalCodeCombination. Reliable Messaging using VANSEnvelope Reliable transport for MedCom FHIR messages SHALL follow the VANSEnvelope specification (Danish). These rules cover envelope acknowledgements; FHIR application acknowledgements are handled separately. MessageIdentifier below means Message/MetaInformation/Identifier . ID Rule VR1.S VANSEnvelope/Message/MetaInformation/Transport/Type SHALL be reliable or omitted (the default) for envelopes carrying FHIR messages. VR2.R The receiver SHALL return a VANSEnvelopeAcknowledgement to the sender VR3.R The receiver SHALL check EnvelopeIdentifier and MessageIdentifier against previously received envelopes. If both are new, it SHALL process the message. VR4.R An unchanged message with a known MessageIdentifier is a duplicate, whether its EnvelopeIdentifier is known or new. VR5.S When retrying an unchanged message, including after a lost acknowledgement, the sender SHALL assign a new EnvelopeIdentifier and dispatch time, retaining the MessageIdentifier and all other content. VR6.S Changed message content SHALL be sent as a new message with new EnvelopeIdentifier , MessageIdentifier , and applicable timestamps. VR7.R A known EnvelopeIdentifier paired with a new MessageIdentifier is an error: envelope identifiers SHALL NOT be reused. The receiver MAY return a negative VANSEnvelopeAcknowledgement. Sending MedCom FHIR messages Sending MedCom FHIR messages over the VANS Network requires the sending system to handle the following: When sending to both primary and cc destinations. A Sending Ecosystem SHALL secure that the MedCom FHIR messages for primary and cc receivers differ on ID's as described in Governance for MedCom FHIR Messaging A Sending Ecosystem MUST ensure that the total size of a MedCom FHIR message, once embedded in a VANSEnvelope, does not exceed 100 MB when sent on the VANS Network. If the size is validated before the message is embedded in a VANSEnvelope, the Sending Ecosystem MAY apply a slightly lower limit to reserve space for the VANSEnvelope overhead and thereby ensure compliance with the 100 MB maximum. Receiving MedCom FHIR messages A Receiving Ecosystem SHALL be able to receive MedCom FHIR messages both as "application/fhir+xml" and "application/fhir+json" A Receiving Ecosystem SHALL be able to handle both primary and cc destinations and route them to the right application.

text: MedComMessagingMessage Base resource for all MedCom messages. Scope and usage MedComMessagingMessage is the common Bundle profile used by MedCom messaging standards. Individual standards specialize it for their clinical content and corresponding MessageHeader profile. The snapshot and constraints below define the required structure. Additional governance The following requirements are not expressed as constraints on this Bundle profile. ID Requirement MSG-04 A MedCom FHIR Message SHALL contain at least two bundled MedComMessagingOrganization resources. MSG-10 With the exception of an acknowledgement message; A MedCom FHIR Message SHALL contain at least one bundled MedComCorePatient resource. Validation before dispatch and before processing received messages is governed by Messaging validation governance . Bundle identifiers and dispatch time Bundle.id corresponds to the EnvelopeId in MedCom OIOXML messages. Each time a message is dispatched, the sender SHALL assign a new globally unique Bundle.id; it SHALL NOT reuse the id of a previously dispatched Bundle. A new Bundle.id does not change the identity of the message carried in the Bundle; see MessageHeader identity . The optional Bundle.identifier can be assigned explicitly by the sending application and MAY have the same value as Bundle.id. Bundle.timestamp records the dispatch time of the message. text: MedComMessagingMessageHeader MessageHeader for MedCom messages Scope and usage MedComMessagingMessageHeader provides the routing and event information for a MedCom message. Individual messaging standards specialize this profile for their events and workflow. Required elements, destination slices, reference types, and narrative requirements are defined in the snapshot and element descriptions below. Message identity and acknowledgements MessageHeader.id corresponds to the LetterId in MedCom OIOXML messages and identifies the message independently of the Bundle used to dispatch it. Its element definition specifies uniqueness for new messages and retention of the id for retransmissions. Carbon copies and forwards are new messages; see copy and forward scenarios . The id is used when describing message history in MedComMessagingProvenance . When processing a message other than an Acknowledgement, the receiving system SHALL return an Acknowledgement whose MessageHeader.response.identifier quotes the request's MessageHeader.id, so the sender can correlate the response with its request. title: MedComMessagingProvenance
text: MedComMessagingProvenance Provenance information about the messages preceeding the current message Scope and usage This profile is used as the Provenance resource for MedCom FHIR messages. The Provenance resource tracks information about the activity what was created, revised, or deleted, while referencing the current message and previous messages if such exist. This is why the Provenance resource is valuable in MedCom messaging. MedComMessagingProvenance describes the activity and history of a message. The element Provenance.agent.who contains information about the organisation that was involved in the activity. The element Provenance.target references the MessageHeader in the current message, this is used to distinguish between current and previous messages. The element Provenance.entity.what references the event that initiated a message e.g., a previous message. The figure below illustrates the references from the Provenance resource. Activity In MedCom messaging, the Provenance.target shall always be a reference to a MedComMessagingMessageHeader or a profile which inherits from / has a base resource of MedComMessagingMessageHeader . The target references the resources on which the new activity has occurred. For instance if Provenance.activity is reply-message , it references a MessageHeader in the Bundle which will point to the contents of the reply. While other Provenances in the bundle, might point to earlier activities, such as the first activtiy new-message which will point to another messageheader that describes the contents of the first message. The activitycodes used to describe the activity of the MedCom message may differ between standard e.g. HospitalNotification and CareCommunication . Due to the different requirements of activities in a standard, it should be expected that there will be different invariants pointing at specific ValueSets for the given standard. Provenance.agent describes the actor who is responsible for the activity that took place, by referencing the organisation responsible for the activity. The referenced organisation shall be an MedComMessagingOrganization . History ID Requirement PROV-02 A MedCom FHIR Message SHALL contain one bundled MedComMessagingProvenance resource for each message exchange the message has been involved in. PROV-03 An Acknowledgement message SHALL contain no more than two bundled MedComMessagingProvenance resources. These history and count requirements are not enforced by this Provenance profile. The Bundle's medcom-messaging-2 constraint already enforces the presence of at least one Provenance resource. MedComMessagingProvenance handles the message history in the Provenance.entity element. This element shall be included if the message is a response to a previous message. In this case the element Provenance.entity.role is used to describe how the entity is used in the message. Provenance.entity.role shall be: revision when a message is a response, a correction, or a forwarding. removal when the message is a cancellation of a previously send message. When a message is a response to a previous message, the previous message shall be referenced from the element Provenance.entity.what. The reference depends on the type of the previous message, which can be a MedCom FHIR message or a EDIFACT/OIOXML message. In the latter case, the reference shall be [lokationsnummer]#[brevid]. Timestamps In MedComMessagingProvenance there are two timestamps, that represents the date and time the message was sent but in two different ways. Provenance.occurredDateTime is a human readable date and time and Provenance.recorded is a machine readable date and time. See the documentation on how to interpret the contents of this table 0 . Provenance Definition Provenance of a resource is a record that describes entities and processes involved in producing and delivering or otherwise influencing that resource. Provenance provides a critical foundation for assessing authenticity, enabling trust, and allowing reproducibility. Provenance assertions are a form of contextual metadata and can themselves become important records with their own provenance. Provenance statement indicates clinical significance in terms of confidence in authenticity, reliability, and trustworthiness, integrity, and stage in lifecycle (e.g. Document Completion - has the artifact been legally authenticated), all of which may impact security, privacy, and trust policies. Short Who, What, When for a set of resources Comments Some parties may be duplicated between the target resource and its provenance. For instance, the prescriber is usually (but not always) the author of the prescription resource. This resource is defined with close consideration for W3C Provenance. title: MedComMessagingRequesterOrganization
text: MedComRequesterOrganization This profile is intended to be used to represent the requester organization of the observations. Note: This profile is intended to represent the requester organization of the observations. The requester can be the a general practitioner, who orders a number of homecare or laboratory observation. Scope and usage This profile is intended to be used to represent the requester organization of the observations. Contact informations It is required to specify contact person at the organization that reqests observations. The contact information shall contain either initials of the general practitioner or status "unknown" from the data-absent-reason ValueSet shall be sent. In MedComMessagingRequesterOrganization the contact.name.given shall be used to express the initials of the general practitioner. The standard follows HL7 rulse to expres initals.
